title: Detection of complex nitrogen-bearing molecule ethyl cyanide towards the hot molecular core G10.47 + 0.03
question: Detect rotational emission lines of ethyl cyanide (C2H5CN) towards the hot molecular core G10.47+0.03, determine its column density, rotational temperature, spatial distribution, and fractional abundance, and investigate its formation mechanism.

what.value: Systemic velocity (V_LSR = 68.50 km s^-1), gas density (7x10^7 cm^-3), and hot core temperature (~150 K / >200 K) of G10.47+0.03

evidence.loc: Identification of C2H5CN towards the G10.47+003
evidence.quote: The systematic velocity ($V_{LSR}$) of the G10.47+0.03 is 68.50 km s$^{-1}$ (cite: rol11).

evidence.loc: Identification of C2H5CN towards the G10.47+003
evidence.quote: The LTE assumption is valid in the warm inner region of G10.47+0.03 because the gas density of the hot core region of G10.47+0.03 is 7$\times$10$^{7}$ cm$^{-3}$ (cite: rol11).

what.value: Hydrogen column density towards G10.47+0.03 (1.35x10^25 cm^-2)

evidence.quote: The fractional abundance of with respect to H$_{2}$ is calculated to be 5.70$\times$10$^{-9}$, and the hydrogen column density towards G10.47+0.03 is calculated to be 1.35$\times$10$^{25}$ cm$^{-2}$ (cite: gor20).

what.value: Spectroscopic molecular database for C2H5CN from Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (CDMS)

evidence.loc: Identification of C2H5CN towards the G10.47+003
evidence.quote: For identification of the rotational emission lines of towards the G10.47+0.03, we use the local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) model with the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (CDMS) (cite: mu05) spectroscopic molecular database.

what.value: Three-phase warm-up chemical modelling abundances of C2H5CN (5.7x10^-9 for fast, 7.7x10^-8 for medium, 3.0x10^-8 for slow warm-up models)

evidence.loc: Comparison with observation and modelled abundance of C2H5CN
evidence.quote: After the chemical modelling, (cite: gar13) estimated that the abundance of was 5.7$\times$10$^{-9}$ for the fast warm-up model, 7.7$\times$10$^{-8}$ for the medium warm-up model, and 3.0$\times$10$^{-8}$ for the slow warm-up model.

recipe.method: Fit a 2D Gaussian over the 16 continuum images to estimate integrated flux density, peak flux density, synthesised beam size, position angle, and RMS
key_parameters: 16 continuum frequencies between 130.234 GHz and 160.155 GHz

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and identify C2H5CN lines via LTE modelling
recipe.method: Extract spectra from a 2.5" diameter circular region and perform LTE spectral modelling using the LTE-RADEX module in CASSIS with the CDMS database
key_parameters: Circular extraction aperture diameter = 2.5" centred at RA = 18h08m38.232s, Dec = -19d51m50.440s
V_LSR = 68.50 km s^-1, source size = 2.5", FWHM = 10.2 km s^-1, T_ex = 300 K
assumptions: Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE) valid due to high gas density of 7x10^7 cm^-3

recipe.goal: Map spatial distribution and measure emitting region size of non-blended C2H5CN transitions
recipe.method: Generate integrated emission (moment 0) maps of the 6 non-blended transitions using CASA task IMMOMENTS and fit 2D Gaussians using IMFIT to derive deconvolved emitting region sizes
assumptions: Deconvolved source size formula theta_S = sqrt(theta_50^2 - theta_beam^2)

recipe.goal: Derive rotational temperature, column density, and fractional abundance via rotational diagram analysis
recipe.method: Fit 1D Gaussian profiles to the non-blended lines using the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm in CASSIS, then perform linear regression on ln(N_u/g_u) vs E_u using the ROTATIONAL DIAGRAM module in CASSIS, and divide column density by N(H2)
key_parameters: 5 of the 6 non-blended lines used in rotational diagram (excluding J = 15(1,15)-14(1,14) due to similar E_up to 15(0,15)-14(0,14))
Partition function Q(T_rot) = 4667.9361 at 75 K, 13209.5867 at 150 K, 37424.5763 at 300 K
assumptions: Optically thin emission and LTE conditions

recipe.goal: Compare derived fractional abundance with three-phase warm-up chemical models
recipe.method: Compare derived fractional abundance X(C2H5CN) = 5.70x10^-9 against the fast, medium, and slow warm-up model predictions of (cite: gar13)
key_parameters: Fast (5x10^4–7.12x10^4 yr), medium (2x10^5–2.85x10^5 yr), and slow (1x10^6–1.43x10^6 yr) warm-up timescales
assumptions: Isothermal free-fall collapse phase (n_H from 3x10^3 to 10^7 cm^-3, T_dust from 16 K to 8 K) followed by static warm-up phase (n_H ~ 10^7 cm^-3, T_dust from 8 K to 400 K)
